input_messages.content: Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would like to get this fixed so I can send picture messages again. Can you help me with that?
Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002. My name is John Smith. Let me know if you need any other information to help with the MMS issue.
I ran the checks you asked for. It says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages. Also, my phone's status bar is showing that Airplane Mode is on, and my battery is at 80%. What should I do next?
I turned off Airplane Mode as you said. Now my phone shows no signal and data is disabled, with the battery still at 80%. What should I do next?
The check says my phone has no SIM card detected. What does that mean? How can I fix it?
I reseated the SIM card as you suggested. Now my phone shows a poor signal with 2G network and data enabled. The SIM card status is active and working. What should I do next?
The network mode preference on my phone is set to 2G only. What should I do to get a faster network for MMS?
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G. Now my phone shows excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. But unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try?
The APN name on my phone is "internet" and the MMSC URL for picture messages is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc". What should I do with this information?
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON on my phone. Should I turn it off to see if that helps with sending MMS?

I turned off Wi-Fi Calling as you suggested. My phone still shows excellent 5G signal and data enabled, but unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? I'm getting a bit frustrated with this.
The messaging app has permission for SMS and phone, but it does not show permission for storage. Should I try to grant the storage permission to the messaging app?
I granted the storage permission to the messaging app as you advised. Now the app can send MMS messages! Thank you for helping me fix this. Is there anything else I should do?

No, that's all for now. Thank you very much for your help and patience with me. I really appreciate it. Have a great day! 

###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles

- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information

- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would like to get this fixed so I can send picture messages again. Can you help me with that?
I can help with that. First I need to identify your account. Can you give me the phone number on your line? If you'd rather, you can give me your full name and date of birth.
Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002. My name is John Smith. Let me know if you need any other information to help with the MMS issue.

Thanks, John. I found your account, and line 555-123-2002 is active. Its data usage is within the plan limit.

Let's run some checks on your phone. Please run **can_send_mms** (the check for whether your messaging app can send MMS) and tell me what it says. Please also run **check_status_bar** and tell me what it shows. That covers signal strength, airplane mode, mobile data, and so on.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I ran the checks you asked for. It says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages. Also, my phone's status bar is showing that Airplane Mode is on, and my battery is at 80%. What should I do next?

Airplane Mode is on, and that blocks cellular service and mobile data. MMS needs both. Please use **toggle_airplane_mode** to turn it OFF. Then run **check_status_bar** again and tell me what it shows now, especially the signal strength and the mobile data status.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I turned off Airplane Mode as you said. Now my phone shows no signal and data is disabled, with the battery still at 80%. What should I do next?

Mobile data is disabled, and there's still no signal. Please run **check_sim_status** and tell me what it shows (for example Active, Missing, or Locked). I'll use that to work out why you have no signal.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
The check says my phone has no SIM card detected. What does that mean? How can I fix it?

The phone isn't detecting the SIM card, which is why you have no signal. The SIM may not be seated properly. Please use **reseat_sim_card**, which simulates removing and reinserting the SIM. Then run **check_sim_status** again and tell me the result.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your SIM card is active and working.
I reseated the SIM card as you suggested. Now my phone shows a poor signal with 2G network and data enabled. The SIM card status is active and working. What should I do next?
The SIM is working now. But 2G is too slow for MMS, which needs at least 3G. Please run **check_network_mode_preference** and tell me what it shows.
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only
The network mode preference on my phone is set to 2G only. What should I do to get a faster network for MMS?

Please use **set_network_mode_preference** and set the mode to **"4g_5g_preferred"**. That lets your phone connect to 4G or 5G. Then run **check_status_bar** again and tell me the signal strength and network type. After that, run **can_send_mms** again to see if MMS works.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G. Now my phone shows excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. But unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try?
Your connection is good now, so the next thing to check is the APN settings, specifically the MMSC URL. Please run **check_apn_settings** and tell me what it shows for the APN name and the MMSC URL.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
The APN name on my phone is "internet" and the MMSC URL for picture messages is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc". What should I do with this information?

The MMSC URL is set, so the APN doesn't look like the cause. Next I want to rule out Wi-Fi Calling, which can interfere with MMS. Please run **check_wifi_calling_status** and tell me whether it shows Wi-Fi Calling as ON or OFF.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON on my phone. Should I turn it off to see if that helps with sending MMS?
Yes, please turn it off. Use **toggle_wifi_calling** to switch Wi-Fi Calling OFF. Then run **can_send_mms** again and tell me whether your messaging app can send MMS now.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I turned off Wi-Fi Calling as you suggested. My phone still shows excellent 5G signal and data enabled, but unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? I'm getting a bit frustrated with this.

I know this is frustrating, and I appreciate your patience. One check is left: the messaging app's permissions. It needs **storage** and **sms** permissions to send MMS.

Please run **check_app_permissions** for the app "messaging" and tell me which permissions it lists as granted.
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.
The messaging app has permission for SMS and phone, but it does not show permission for storage. Should I try to grant the storage permission to the messaging app?

Yes. Storage is missing, and the app needs it to access your picture and video files. Please use **grant_app_permission** with app_name "messaging" and permission "storage". Then run **can_send_mms** again and tell me whether MMS works now.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.
I granted the storage permission to the messaging app as you advised. Now the app can send MMS messages! Thank you for helping me fix this. Is there anything else I should do?

Good news that MMS works again. You don't need to do anything else. I changed several things along the way: Airplane Mode off, SIM reseated, network mode set to 4G/5G preferred, Wi-Fi Calling off, and storage permission granted to the messaging app. You can leave them as they are.

If you have more problems later, contact us again. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

No, that's all for now. Thank you very much for your help and patience with me. I really appreciate it. Have a great day! 

###STOP###
